solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Physician became dictator's prisoner

indicators.note: a prisoner is held inside, so the answer is held captive within the run of words

blocks.note: the letters straddling the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A doctor who rose to become a tyrant's captive, or a tyrant himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across becaME DICtator.
explanation.definitionFit: A medic is an informal word for a doctor or other medical practitioner.

clue.text: Resistance from foreign noble deprived of his own?

indicators.note: deprived means stripped of something, so the noble loses a letter of his own title

blocks.note: a French or continental nobleman ranking above a count

explanation.surface: An aristocrat abroad stripped of his estates joins the underground, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The French marquis drops an R; the question mark owns up to the loose way the lost letter is indicated, and hints that the fighters too had lost their own country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maquis were the French guerrilla fighters of the Second World War, and the word stands for that underground movement.

clue.text: Wilde resorted to this club after eventful year

indicators.note: after sends the club to follow the eventful word when the pieces are joined

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde reaching for a weapon after a turbulent twelve months.
explanation.walkthrough: The club follows eventful but comes before year in the answer; the definition is a description of the device Wilde favoured, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde's plays lean heavily on the device where the audience knows what a character does not.

clue.text: Fine provincial force once set up court abroad

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised from bottom to top, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as the letter I
the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police until 2001

explanation.surface: An old provincial constabulary erecting a court somewhere foreign, perhaps with a fine imposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is often called the Province, hence provincial force. A1RUC read upwards gives CURIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Curia is the papal court in Rome, and in ancient Rome a curia was a senate house or court.

clue.text: Do too little work and prepare to play, given the chance

definitions.text: prepare to play, given the chance

blocks.clueFragment: prepare to play, given the chance
blocks.note: second meaning: to learn a role so as to stand in for the lead actor

explanation.surface: A lazy student who still hopes to be picked for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word into UNDER + STUDY, as if studying too little.
explanation.definitionFit: An understudy learns another actor's part so as to perform it if the lead falls ill or cannot appear.

clue.text: Politician needs support of course within global alliance — plenty given

indicators.note: within places these pieces inside the alliance's letters

blocks.note: the peg supporting a golf ball on the course

explanation.surface: A politician seeks backing within an international body that has resources to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: Support of course is golfing language: the course is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word for a large but unspecified number, so very many or plenty.

clue.text: Drink, getting into gear before lecture?

indicators.note: before tells us which piece is placed first when the two are joined

blocks.note: putting on clothes, gear being clothing
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: Having a quick drink while getting changed before giving a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue as drink then dressing, but before puts the dressing first.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing-down is a severe reprimand, a telling-off of the kind a lecture can be.

clue.text: One sorcerer with scarlet cloak portrayed again

indicators.note: a cloak wraps around its wearer, so the scarlet word goes round the others

explanation.surface: A wizard in a red cape, depicted once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Mage is an old literary word for a magician; cloak here wraps the colour round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimagine or re-image something is to depict it afresh, to represent it in a new way.

clue.text: Pinch mistress's bottom in gallery

indicators.note: the bottom of a word in a down clue is its final letter
in places the selected letter inside the gallery's name

blocks.note: the Tate, the London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone groping a woman's behind in an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cheeky misdirection: Pinch is a small amount, and the Tate is the famous London gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinch of salt and a taste of something are both a tiny quantity, a little sample.

clue.text: A top-of-range gadget for boxer's trainer, perhaps

definitions.text: A top-of-range gadget for boxer's trainer, perhaps

blocks.clueFragment: A top-of-range gadget for boxer's trainer
blocks.note: surface reading: the best equipment a boxing coach can buy
setter's reading: a device sounding at the very top of the pitch range, used to train a boxer, the breed of dog

explanation.walkthrough: Boxer and top-of-range both mislead: the boxer is a dog, and the range is of sound pitch, too high for human ears.
explanation.definitionFit: This high-pitched whistle is audible to canine ears but not human ones, and owners use it in obedience training.

clue.text: Ran through party on purpose

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, setting the order of the pieces

blocks.note: the use or point of something
the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone dashing through a celebration deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: Party is not the usual DO here but Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionists.
explanation.definitionFit: To run through money or supplies is to exhaust them completely, leaving them all consumed.

clue.text: Run in to rouse support for equestrian

indicators.note: in puts the running letter inside the word for rouse

blocks.note: to stir up is to rouse or provoke

explanation.surface: Running in to wake someone and get help for a rider.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal loop hung from a saddle supports a rider's foot, so it supports the horseman.

clue.text: Oppressive form of greeting rebounded on Scot?

indicators.note: something that rebounds comes back the way it came, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: a typically Scottish first name; the question mark shows it is one example

explanation.surface: A harsh kind of greeting that bounced back on a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords use Ian, Mac or Jock for a Scot; here the name is the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian means excessively harsh, after Draco, the Athenian lawgiver whose penalties were notoriously severe.

clue.text: Ruined city's favourite artist

blocks.note: a teacher's pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Someone naming the painter they love best from a ruined city.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Petra is the ancient rock-cut city in Jordan, now an abandoned archaeological site of ruins.

clue.text: Stormy petrels in Times account may attract it

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent and tossed about, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Seabirds in rough weather reported in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Times looks like the newspaper but is just fodder; the definition is a description, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A savings account may earn a basic kind of return calculated only on the original principal, not compounded.

clue.text: As fruit, cut by length four times

indicators.note: a thing cut by something has that something driven into it, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: Latin for in the capacity of, as
a stone fruit such as a plum

explanation.surface: Fruit sliced lengthwise into four portions.
explanation.walkthrough: Qua, as in a man qua man, means in the role of; a drupe is a botanist's word for a fruit with a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Quadruple means multiplied by four, fourfold, as when a price quadruples.

clue.text: Is financing it in a new way not worth considering?

indicators.note: doing something in a new way means rearranging it, here the letters

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A question about whether a novel way of funding a project is negligible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insignificant is too small or unimportant to merit attention or concern.

clue.text: Confused report of more profound times

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so we want what the following words sound like

blocks.note: inner means deeper, more profound; days are times

explanation.surface: Bewildered by an account of deeper eras.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent inner days and the answer are said identically.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a daze means stunned or bewildered, unable to think clearly, so muddled.

clue.text: Holes in long-haul craft

explanation.surface: An aircraft on a long-distance flight with holes in it.
explanation.walkthrough: In looks like a container indicator, but it is a piece meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel built for travel through outer space covers the longest hauls of all.

clue.text: Chief heading off westward quaffing island's wine

indicators.note: the head of the word comes off, so its first letter is dropped
in an across clue westward is right to left, so the remaining letters read backwards
quaffing means drinking down, so the island letter is swallowed inside

explanation.surface: A leader heading west, drinking an islander's wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white Spanish wine from the region of that name in northern Spain.

clue.text: Couturier's accessories causing a sensation

blocks.note: first meaning: the sewing kit a dressmaker uses
second meaning: the prickling felt when a numb limb recovers

explanation.surface: A fashion designer's accessories make a big splash.
explanation.walkthrough: A sensation suggests a triumph on the catwalk, but it is a physical feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a tailor's sewing tools and the tingling feeling when circulation returns.

clue.text: Liquid (black) in small vault whence pong emanates

indicators.note: in places the liquid and black inside the vault

explanation.surface: Black liquid stored in a little crypt, the source of a nasty smell.
explanation.walkthrough: Pong is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A stink bomb is a small device that releases a foul-smelling gas when broken, as a prank.

clue.text: Can't grasp what happens during fall

blocks.note: first meaning: releases hold, lets go
second meaning: in autumn the foliage departs from the trees

explanation.walkthrough: Fall is the American word for autumn; to leave go is a British colloquialism for let go.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leaves go has released their hold, and in autumn the foliage drops from branches.

clue.text: Detecting online espionage?

explanation.surface: Uncovering cyber-espionage.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as e-spying, internet espionage; the question mark flags the invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of or notice, so espying means spotting or detecting.

clue.text: Bird we're told put six feet under bush

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so we want a word that sounds the same

explanation.surface: A bird buried beneath a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The gooseberry is a thorny shrub grown for its sour green fruit, so a bush.

clue.text: Recidivist bets on queen wearing hat

indicators.note: in a down clue something wearing a hat sits under it, so the hat comes first

blocks.note: to back a horse is to bet on it

explanation.surface: A repeat offender gambling on a monarch in a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, the queen wearing a hat sits beneath it; ER is the crossword queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A recidivist relapses into crime, and a backslider relapses into bad habits.

clue.text: Trouble after an invention puts off Tesla's foremost supporter

indicators.note: foremost means the very front, so only the first letter of the name is wanted
to put something off is to discard it, so that letter is removed
after places the trouble word at the end of the answer

blocks.note: first letter of the inventor's name

explanation.surface: An invention disappoints Nikola Tesla's chief backer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla the inventor makes invention look like a definition, but it means a made-up story.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is a keen and knowledgeable enthusiast, a fan or devoted supporter.

clue.text: Note: United explicit about player making a pile

explanation.surface: A memo saying a football club has openly backed a player who is earning a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Making a pile suggests getting rich, but an atomic pile was an early name for this device.
explanation.definitionFit: The first nuclear reactors were called atomic piles because they were built from stacked graphite blocks.

clue.text: Normal rugged sort: old actor

indicators.note: rugged means rough and uneven, so the preceding word is roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: An ordinary weathered type who is getting on.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon divides the wordplay from the definition; old gives a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlon Brando was the American screen star of On the Waterfront and The Godfather.

clue.text: One detective force intercepts sovereign trying to kill his relative?

indicators.note: to intercept is to come between, so these pieces break into the sovereign word

explanation.surface: Police stop a monarch plotting to murder a member of his family.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads back to the sovereign: a would-be killer of a king who is his relative, as in Shakespeare's histories.
explanation.definitionFit: Regicidal means relating to or bent on killing a king, here a royal relation of the murderer.

clue.text: Stimulant mostly taken after capital pasta

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter goes
taken after puts the stimulant behind the capital city

explanation.surface: A drug consumed after a pasta dish in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni is an Italian pasta made in short ridged tubes, a familiar kind of pasta shape.

clue.text: Find fault with batsman's innings

blocks.note: first meaning: to criticise or disparage
second meaning: a cricketer's stint at the crease

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman's innings is informally called by this word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to criticise or belittle, and the noun is cricket slang for a spell of batting.

clue.text: Collaborator getting slower taken in by shrink

indicators.note: taken in means swallowed or absorbed, so the slower word goes inside

blocks.note: ritardando, the musical direction to slow down

explanation.surface: A partner who is slowing down is being treated by a psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrink looks like a psychiatrist; here it is the verb meaning flinch.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-writer shares the work of writing a book or song, so works jointly as a collaborator.

clue.text: Sound measure by which to rank European city

explanation.surface: A reliable gauge for ranking cities in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Sound looks like an adjective meaning reliable but is about loudness.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade is the capital of Serbia, standing where the Sava meets the Danube.

clue.text: Moving ceremony to celebrate engagement

explanation.surface: A touching church ceremony held to mark a betrothal.
explanation.walkthrough: Engagement suggests a wedding to come, but it means military combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Active service is duty with armed forces in operations against an enemy, as in an engagement or battle.

clue.text: Spooner's assessing safe charging point for motorist

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds here are exchanged

blocks.note: marking is assessing; a peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: Spooner checking whether a roadside charging point is safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is thieves' slang for a safe. Charging point suggests electric cars, but the charge is a fee for leaving the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated device at the kerb charges a motorist for the time a car stays parked there.

clue.text: No clergy, only Mae West in disguise

indicators.note: a disguise changes appearance, so the letters take on a new arrangement

explanation.surface: No priests allowed, just the film star Mae West dressed up.
explanation.walkthrough: Mae West, the actress, is a decoy: only her surname's initial is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Laywomen are female members of a church who are not ordained, so they are not clergy.

clue.text: German governor critical after contrary strike

indicators.note: contrary means the opposite way round, so the word for strike is read backwards
after places critical behind the reversed strike word

blocks.note: to ram is to strike hard

explanation.surface: A German official in a serious state after a contrary walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike looks like industrial action, but it means hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A margrave was the military governor of a German border province in the Holy Roman Empire.

clue.text: Attractive female player's first to go in eliminator

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the player word
to go means to depart, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a cup tie is a knockout match in a football competition

explanation.surface: A glamorous footballer is the first to be dropped for a knockout game.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football a cup tie is a knockout match, where the loser is eliminated.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is an informal word for an attractive person, especially a pretty young woman.

clue.text: Canny, by the way?

blocks.note: first meaning: shrewd, wise to the ways of the world
second meaning, read literally: in the manner of a road, the suffix -wise meaning with regard to

explanation.walkthrough: By the way looks like an aside, but read literally a way is a road, so it means in road terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone streetwise is shrewd about the hazards of urban life, and canny means astute.

clue.text: Thought's being restricted again, as it were

definitions.text: being restricted again, as it were

blocks.clueFragment: being restricted again, as it were
blocks.note: second meaning: the undoing of a release

explanation.walkthrough: The second half invents a word: if liberation frees you, de-liberation would lock you up again, and as it were owns up to the coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberation is long and careful consideration before deciding, so it is thought.

clue.text: Mincing man with poodle ridiculed

indicators.note: mincing means chopping finely, so the letters are cut up and remixed

explanation.surface: An affected, prancing man with a fancy dog was mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: Mincing reads as a description of a man's walk, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon someone is to satirise them publicly, mocking them with ridicule.

clue.text: Potential catch by fishing port barely mentioned

blocks.note: a flat fish an angler might land
the Kent port, home of the Dover sole

explanation.surface: A fish that might be landed near a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is the English Channel port in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: To skate over a topic is to pass over it quickly, mentioning it only in passing.

clue.text: Spades and fork, rough but penetrating

blocks.note: a three-pronged spear, like a fork

explanation.surface: Garden tools that are crude but cut deep into the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: Spades and fork look like a gardener's kit, but spades is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice is loud and harsh, grating yet carrying far, so rough but piercing.

clue.text: Search suspect, male, ahead of time

explanation.surface: Police frisk a male suspect before time runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: Suspect looks like a noun but is the adjective: rum is British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: To rummage is to hunt through things untidily, so to search for something.

clue.text: Even dons like exams

indicators.note: to don is to put on clothing, so one word is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: as, in the sense of similar to

explanation.surface: University lecturers who enjoy examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: Dons look like Oxbridge tutors, but the word means puts on. A levels are the English school-leaving exams taken at eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A levels are the advanced exams English pupils sit at eighteen for university entrance.

clue.text: Philosopher Latinises text I mistranslated

indicators.note: a mistranslation garbles the original, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A thinker renders a document into Latin and gets it wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Sartre and Kierkegaard were thinkers of the school that stresses individual freedom and choice.

clue.text: Drive time's up, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: A driving lesson or test cut short by the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force or motivation that pushes something forward, so a drive or momentum.

clue.text: Cavalier almost impaling himself, in brief

indicators.note: something impaled is run through, so one word is pierced by the other and sits within it

blocks.note: the abbreviation for the cavalier himself

explanation.surface: A cavalier nearly running himself through.
explanation.walkthrough: Himself points back to the definition: the abbreviation for the answer, as in a title, is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier was a mounted soldier, and the word comes from the same root as chevalier, a mounted knight.

clue.text: It often goes with "cheers", and audible countercheers

indicators.note: audible means heard, so we want the word that sounds like the following

explanation.surface: A toast is answered with jeers.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheers is said when raising a glass, so the definition is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcohol is what people usually hold when they say cheers as a toast.

clue.text: Writer rejected one indoor game for another

indicators.note: rejected suggests sent back, so the writer word reads backwards

explanation.surface: An author turned down one parlour game in favour of a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: one indoor game gives the letters, and another means a second indoor game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a game of numbered cards played in halls, so another indoor pastime.

clue.text: Teach music abroad, ditching posh teaching method

indicators.note: ditching means throwing away, so the letter for posh is removed
abroad means scattered widely, so the letters spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A music teacher working overseas drops the upmarket approach.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechism teaches religious doctrine through a fixed set of questions and answers.

clue.text: Juvenile journalist particularly cut up

blocks.note: a cub reporter is a novice

explanation.surface: A young reporter who is especially upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut up looks like distressed, but it is chopping food in a particular shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubed food is chopped into small square pieces, one particular way of cutting it.

clue.text: Scoffer joins press, producing crude output

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: A cynic joins a newspaper and turns out vulgar copy.
explanation.walkthrough: Scoffer suggests a mocker and press a newspaper; both mislead. To scoff is British slang for eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig iron is the impure metal first produced by a blast furnace, before refining.

clue.text: Red Guard primarily holds sway, having ousted leader

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so only the opening letter of the guard is used
ousting the leader replaces the first letter of the sway word

explanation.surface: A Red Army guard seizes power after deposing the leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The guard's letter takes the place of the first letter of the ruling word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gules is the heraldic term for the colour red on a coat of arms.

clue.text: Not being alone at work is essential

indicators.note: at work means being worked on, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Having company in the workplace is vital.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is not open to discussion or compromise must be had, so it is required.

clue.text: Coming to littl'un exhausted granny to start with

indicators.note: to start with picks out the first letter of the granny word

explanation.surface: A toddler wears out grandma first of all.
explanation.walkthrough: Coming to suggests waking up, but it means amounting to, as a bill comes to a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill totalling fifty pounds comes to fifty pounds: both mean adding up to a sum.

clue.text: Cover for Oriental bowl of some antiquity

indicators.note: a cover goes round the outside, so only the outer letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A lid for an antique Chinese bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover for looks like a lid but takes the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something oldish is fairly aged without being ancient, so it has a degree of age.

clue.text: Top working girl in bodyguard benefits initially

indicators.note: in places the working girl inside the bodyguard letters

explanation.surface: A senior escort among the protection officers gets the perks first.
explanation.walkthrough: The SS began as Hitler's personal bodyguard; benefits initially is the definition, not a first-letter instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is an advantage given at the outset of a race or contest, a benefit at the beginning.

clue.text: Son in confinement lashed out

indicators.note: in places the son beside the confinement word, son first

blocks.note: pent, as in pent up, means confined

explanation.surface: A son in prison who struck out violently.
explanation.walkthrough: Lashed out looks violent but means splashed out money; in looks like a container but here just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out on something is British slang for spending money freely, so to have spent.
